subject: chemistry
title: Lattice Light: Born-Haber Cycles
welcome_lead: Build Born-Haber cycles to find lattice enthalpies.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on Born-Haber cycle construction.
final_note: You traced ions from atoms to lattice.

concepts.def: Energy to form 1 mol ionic lattice from gas ions.
Energy to make 1 mol gaseous atoms.
Energy to remove e- from gas atom.
Energy when 1 mol e- added to gas atoms.
Cycle linking ΔHf and lattice enthalpy.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Steps: Na(s) -> Na(g) (atomisation +108); Na(g) -> Na+(g) + e- (1st IE +496); 1/2 Cl2(g) -> Cl(g) (atomisation +122); Cl(g) + e- -> Cl-(g) (EA -349); Na+(g) + Cl-(g) -> NaCl(s) (lattice).

Sum equals ΔHf(NaCl) = -411 kJ/mol. Rearrange to solve for lattice enthalpy.

Atomisation, IE: positive (endothermic). EA: usually negative for first e-.

Lattice enthalpy (formation route): negative (exothermic). Lattice dissociation: positive.

Apply Hess: ΔHf = sum of step enthalpies. Solve for unknown step.

For NaCl: -411 = 108 + 496 + 122 + (-349) + LE -> LE = -788 kJ/mol.

mcqs.q: What state are the ions in when defining lattice enthalpy of formation?
options: The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
The ions are in aqueous solution before forming the lattice.
Gaseous ions — lattice enthalpy is the energy change when one mole of solid ionic compound forms from its constituent ions in the GAS phase.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.

mcqs.q: Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.
If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.
The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
